title: How much should you bet? Kelly's answer

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You win a bet half the time, and it pays one and a half times your stake. How much of your money should you put down each round? Too little and you leave growth on the table. Too much and you can lose even though the odds favour you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds backwards. Is there an actual answer?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There is, and it's called the Kelly criterion. It sets the bet size from two things, the probability of winning and the payoff ratio. Kelly_RM is an AlgoÉTS research repository that lets you watch the rule at work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First with a coin-flip game. A biased coin, repeated bets, and four bettors side by side. One bets the Kelly fraction. One waits ten flips, then bets on the frequency it has observed. One bets a fixed amount. And one bets big after three tails in a row.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what happens to the Kelly bettor?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the notebook's example, with five hundred dollars to start and ten flips, the Kelly fraction works out to one sixth. So the first bet is about eighty-three dollars. Growth per flip is around two percent.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if you bet more than that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the surprise. At twice the Kelly fraction, growth falls to zero. Beyond that, wealth shrinks over time, even though every single flip has a positive expected value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it moves to real markets?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. A second notebook downloads price histories, uses the first three years to optimise an RSI strategy for each ticker, then keeps the unseen data apart. From the trades, it works out each ticker's win probability and the size of its wins and losses, and plugs them into the Kelly formula.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. The coin game is described as companion code for a video on the Kelly criterion, which makes it a gentle way in. The written page has the growth table and the flow from ticker to Kelly fraction.
